methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Growth → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.2x) to $10M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Robotics & Manufacturing (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 11 same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Emelody, a Growth-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Jon Thomas and Elizabeth Johnson, has raised $10M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comp universe of nine private robotics firms and one public company (277810.KQ), though narrow-stage peer multiples are constrained by limited comparable data within the same funding tier and stage.

Given sparse Growth-stage comparables in Robotics & Manufacturing, only the Stage-Progression method yielded a reliable signal. Using the $10M total raised as a valuation proxy and applying a 1.2x step-up multiplier typical of Growth stage transitions produced an implied value of $12M. Peer-Median analysis was not applicable; while 11 same-sector peers exist, fewer than three met narrow filters for stage and valuation tier, making a median peer multiple unreliable.

The triangulation supports a valuation range of $10M to $14M, with a median of $12M. This narrow one-method result carries material uncertainty. Key risks include the sparsity of direct Growth-stage comps, reliance on a raised-capital proxy rather than revenue or profitability benchmarks, and the heterogeneity of robotics subsectors. Refinement would benefit from revenue multiples or a deeper comparable set at the same stage.
